pageCache.text:
In year admissions (current years 7-11)
We welcome applications to the school for in-year entry. The school is usually oversubscribed and, should the school not be in a position to offer a place, a waiting list is held, ranked in accordance with the published oversubscription criteria. Places can only be offered if we are under our planned admission number (PAN) for the year the application is being requested or if a place becomes available due to a student leaving.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application within 10 working days of the receipt of application.
How to apply
To make an in-year application you will need to complete our Supplementary Admission form and the Kent In Year Admission Form. Please return the completed forms to the Admissions Office at the school address or emailed to [email protected].
Please contact the school if you require a hard copy of the forms.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance at Bennett - Bennett Memorial Diocesan School

Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance at Bennett
Our Vision for Careers Education at Bennett
In addition to encouraging students to think about their future pathways, Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) provides an invaluable opportunity for us to motivate and inspire our young people to fulfil their potential. This is why CEIAG is embedded within every key stage at Bennett. We are committed to providing students in our care with the very best educational opportunities, helping guide them to make the very best possible choices with regards to their personal, social and educational development. We want all of our young people to be equipped to make wider contributions to our local community and wider society and to make informed decisions about their future education, training and career pathways. Our CEIAG aims to promote equality of opportunity at every stage.
At all points, our careers education at Bennett aims to allow all students to make a positive contribution, feel valued and cared for as individuals and be well-informed about their options at each stage of their school life. Careers education is ambitious for our students. We place particular emphasis on ensuring that students can access fully impartial advice with our careers officer, Mrs Paton-Philip, and have access to a wide range of external providers. We seek to engage with the wider community, offering students experiences and advice from a range of employers and education providers in our local community and beyond. We have developed our careers programme to comply with the Gatsby Benchmarks, which set the standard for high quality careers provision in school.
Our Aims for Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance at Bennett:

pageCache.pageTitle: A Level and L3 Diploma Results – August 2026 - Bennett Memorial Diocesan School
pageCache.text:
A Level and L3 Diploma Results – August 2026
Students and staff at Bennett Memorial Diocesan School are again celebrating a set of exceptional A level and Level 3 Diploma results, with students achieving outstanding grades and going on to top universities and other highly sought-after destinations. This cohort of Bennett students have secured the school’s most impressive outcomes in recent history, with our highest ever average point score.
In the large and inclusive sixth form of this outstanding Church of England school, 198 students took A Levels and diplomas this year. The pass rate was exceptional with 99.5% of all examinations passed. 25% of all A Levels taken were passed with grades A*-A, 55%with grades A*- B, and 82% were passed with grades A* to C. Most importantly, the overwhelming majority of students making higher education applications have secured places at universities of their choice, including some of the most prestigious in the country.
Headteacher Karen Brookes said: “We are very proud of the achievements of each and every one of our Bennett students this year. They have achieved excellent results once again right across the board, for which they have worked extraordinarily hard. I would like to offer our students my warmest congratulations and, on their behalf, thank all their teachers for their contribution to making these results possible. I would also like to extend my thanks to all the parents and support staff, without whose guidance and care, none of this would be possible.”
Some outstanding examples, amongst very many others, include:

Dr Brookes continued: “Alongside these, and all other students with A* and A grades, there are many other excellent sets of results, including many which represent significant achievements for the students concerned. It is particularly good to see the strength of these results right across the curriculum, with superb results in natural sciences, psychology and mathematics enabling students to access medicine, engineering, mathematics, psychology and science degrees.
We were particularly pleased to see that our value-added score of +0.32 last year meant that sixth form students at Bennett made more progress than students at any other state funded school in Kent, including all of the grammar schools. Our value-added score for 2026 indicates that even more progress has been made by Bennett students this year.
I am full of admiration for the successes achieved by our Bennett students. Young people are now often given lots of labels and are portrayed quite negatively in the media. However, it is apparent to me that the students we see at Bennett are incredibly resilient, strong, inquisitive and questioning. There is a deep sense that they want to go out and make a difference; be part of building a better society. Those qualities are less easy to label, but perhaps bolder than ever in recent years.
We wish Bennett graduates this year every success as they celebrate the result of their hard work and start the next exciting chapter of their lives.”
If you are interested in joining the Bennett Sixth Form in 2027, you are warmly invited to attend the Sixth Form Open Evening on Wednesday 11th November, 2026.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bennett Music Academy - Bennett Memorial Diocesan School
pageCache.text:
Bennett Music Academy
The ability, joy and excitement in playing an instrument or singing, will stay with you for the rest of your life.
Bennett Music Academy provides outstanding opportunities for all students to learn to play an instrument, to sing and/or perform, under the artistic direction and leadership of the Director of Music. Teaching staff are all currently working professional musicians, both nationally and some internationally and who have a passion for teaching.
Bennett Music Academy fees for all instrumental/vocal lessons are fixed at £220 per term for ten, 30 minute lessons.
Please click here for an application form for music lessons
(Students who take GCSE or A Level examinations during the Summer term will still be eligible for music lessons throughout the exam period. Mesaures are taken to ensure that dates and times of lessons are suitable for the student. Continuing music lessons during the exam season is truly beneficial, providing students with a different enviornment from revision, generating rest and relaxation during a seemingly stressful period.)Music bursaries are also available – View our Bursary Policy on our Policies Page to find out more.
Tuition offered includes: Violin, Viola, Cello, Double Bass, Flute, Oboe, Clarinet, Bassoon, Saxophone, Trumpet, French Horn, Trombone, Euphonium, Tuba, Recorder, Percussion (+ drum kit), Piano, Organ, Guitar (acoustic and/or rock), and singing.(All lesson times are rotated weekly, to faciliate curriculum time.)
Click here to view the Music Department Development Plan 24-2025
We will teach and coach to outstanding, ensuring that all students experience excellence, quality and innovative music making, providing continual performance platform opportunities for everyone to achieve.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE results 2026 - Bennett Memorial Diocesan School
pageCache.text:
GCSE results 2026
Students at Bennett have once again performed exceptionally strongly at GCSE with excellent progress being made by students right across the year group. Bennett is an outstanding, comprehensive, Church of England school, that offers a traditional curriculum of high value subjects, with the vast majority of students successfully completing the English Baccalaureate, which represents a genuine challenge.
This year, 80% of students have achieved 5 or more grades 9-4 including English and maths and 60% have achieved grades 9-5 in both English and mathematics. Two thirds of all grades awarded to this cohort of 296 students were grades 9-5, and a quarter of Bennett GCSE entries were awarded at grades 9-7
Headteacher Karen Brookes said: “I would like to congratulate all Bennett students on their fantastic GCSE results this year. It should be remembered that this is a cohort who saw their studies at the end of KS2 and in the foundational years of KS3 profoundly disrupted by the pandemic. I am full of admiration for the way in which they have approached their studies. Collectively and individually, they have done superbly, laying really strong foundations for their next steps which promise to be very exciting.”
“We are particularly pleased to see once again the exceptionally strong results across the board in English, mathematics, the sciences and languages, alongside the outstanding results in the creative subjects, with large numbers of students achieving the top grades 8 and 9. Students have worked exceptionally hard and these results are a tribute to their commitment and endeavour. These excellent results provide the strong foundations for the next stages of academic study, enabling students to study sought after subjects at A level and beyond Amongst these results are some exceptional individual stories of students coming from disadvantaged backgrounds and overcoming considerable adversity to achieve extraordinary outcomes.”
Amongst the very many stand out results, the following students all achieved seven or more grades 9-7:
“I would like to take this opportunity to thank teachers and other staff who have taught and supported students so effectively, and also parents who play a key role in supporting and encouraging students throughout their school lives.”
“A Bennett education is a fully rounded education, which entails personal development and the formation of character. Opportunities to serve and volunteer are abundant because of the school’s unshakeably clear and Christian character and ethos. Thus the excellent academic outcomes achieved by our students should be read alongside their wider development, with large numbers in this cohort having completed the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme at Bronze level alongside their GCSEs. Indeed our commitment to developing students’ character, values, grit and determination, all within a Christian ethos, is what helps to make these achievements possible.”
We wish all our Bennett students well in their next steps and, of course, look forward to seeing the vast majority in the coming academic year as they return to study here following these excellent GCSE results.
If you are interested in your child joining Bennett Memorial Diocesan School in 2027, you are warmly invited to attend one of the Open Evenings on Tuesday 22nd September or Thursday 24th September, 2026.

Curriculum
Curriculum at Bennett Memorial
At Bennett we enable all of our students to access a broad curriculum of traditional subjects. This is because teaching these subjects means that students can learn the important public knowledge which these subjects embody and which underpins strong intellectual growth and the acquisition of our shared culture. The curriculum must induct children into a level of understanding that allows them to think beyond their own experiences and to learn the powerful knowledge which provides the building blocks for human advancement.
Our curriculum is designed to be challenging and aspirational and, as such it embodies our high aspirations for all our students and is the most powerful tool we have available in our efforts to help them achieve those aspirations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-curricular Sport - Bennett Memorial Diocesan School
pageCache.text:
Extra-curricular Sport
At Bennett we believe strongly in developing the whole person, body and mind. We strongly believe in the positive benefits of exercise, both for developing co-ordination, a healthy body, an active and enquiring mind and teamwork skills. Studies have linked physical activity and good aerobic fitness with good school grades. In an increasingly pressured academic environment we understand the importance of being able to let off steam in organised exercise and competitive sport. We have developed a comprehensive and varied range of extra-curricular activities to suit all aptitudes and interests.
For those interested in highly competitive sports, we have our elite teams of rugby and netball, under the guidance of Mr Singleton (rugby, in conjunction with TWRFC and Mrs Kate Watts (Netball). All students in years 7 and 8 have opportunities to take part in trials for these teams. Students are then grouped into our rugby and netball academies, these students train each a week and play to a high level locally, as do our older students who continue to play throughout their school careers. Our football is also of the highest standard, with teams in each year group.
For those who prefer more recreational sport, there is table tennis club, 2K challenge running club and basketball club. To simply keep fit, students can try out our well-equipped fitness suite or combine fitness with fun by getting involved in our rowing club intra school league. For those with a more aesthetic focus there are our trampoline club and dance club. There is a chance for students to perform at our annual dance show. Our programme is growing all the time, as we introduce new opportunities, and as the seasons change so does the programme; from football and rugby to cricket, tennis and rounders, there is always something active and exciting going on at break and at lunch.
We also offer all students the chance to compete in the inter guild competition that runs throughout the year, culminating in the year’s finale at our annual sports day. We are keen to develop our students in the areas of leadership and coaching and volunteering for sport at all levels. There are various opportunities for students from writing team match reports, to acting as line judges, score keepers or assistant coaches for younger year groups. Sport is high on our list of priorities. Under constant review on our School Improvement Plan, we are always seeking new opportunities to get our students active and involved, and working to improve and develop our facilities. Please review what we have to offer; we are interested in your feedback, and if you would be interested in helping out as a volunteer with one of our activities, please don’t hesitate to contact us.

Appeals
If you have not been offered a place at The Bennett Memorial Diocesan School, the law entitles you to appeal against that decision to an Independent Appeal Panel. This panel is completely independent of the school and the Local Authority. The appeals are held at the school.
If you wish to appeal, please download the appeals form below. Please DO NOT use the Kent County Council form.
You should include any evidence or supporting material with your appeal form and you MUST give the grounds for your appeal at the time you lodge your appeal form. Your appeal form will not be accepted unless you state the grounds for your appeal. You may appeal for more than one school.
